documents.title: Medication Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Renewal request from his pharmacy, lisinopril 20 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg, 90-day supplies. Daughter listed as alternate contact for pickup. Labs current. Approved by PCP, sent with 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3-month follow-up, wife with him.

Wife reports things have been steady since December: same forgetfulness and slowness getting started, no further sudden change. He walks with her most afternoons. Takes his pills from the box she sets up. Eating and sleeping fine. No falls, no new weakness or speech trouble.

BP at goal. Weight unchanged. Pleasant, a bit flat. Mild left drift unchanged. Gait steady.

1. Vascular dementia: stable by family report. Continue routine and supervision.
2. Right frontal ischemic stroke: lisinopril and atorvastatin.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril 20; BMP today.
4. HLD: atorvastatin 40.
Neurology recheck around May/June. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Normal electrolytes and kidney function. No change.

reports.text: CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: acute vertigo, ataxia. Comparison 11/17/2025. Findings: Small well-circumscribed hypodensity in the right frontal lobe, unchanged, consistent with old infarct. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect. Posterior fossa without hemorrhage or hydrocephalus; fourth ventricle midline. No extra-axial collection.
reports.conclusion: No hemorrhage. Old right frontal infarct, unchanged.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PHYSICIAN RECORD, regional hospital (date of service 6/1/2026)

CC: dizziness and nausea

HPI: 69M with HTN, HLD, right frontal ischemic stroke 5/2025 and vascular dementia, brought by wife. Abrupt onset this morning of spinning dizziness with nausea and difficulty staying upright. The spinning persists whether he lies still or fixes on something. Mild headache started at about the same time. No fall, no head injury, did not pass out. History partly from wife given his cognitive impairment.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.
PSH: cataract surgery 2021.
FH: father ischemic stroke at 74, mother HTN, brother CAD.
SH: retired accountant; quit smoking 2017 after 35 pack-years; alcohol rarely.

Vitals: BP 160/90, HR 78, T 36.8 C.
Exam: Horizontal nystagmus that persists with visual fixation. Speech mildly slurred, language intact. Dysmetria on right finger-to-nose. No facial asymmetry, no pronator drift.

CT head noncontrast: no hemorrhage; old right frontal infarct unchanged.
Labs: CBC, BMP, INR unremarkable.

Assessment: acute vertigo with nystagmus not suppressed by fixation, dysarthria and right-sided dysmetria; concern for central (posterior circulation) cause.
Plan: admit for MRI and stroke care.

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

reports.text: MRI BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: acute vertigo, dysmetria. Comparison CT 6/1/2026. Technique: multiplanar multisequence imaging including diffusion-weighted images. Findings: Small focus of restricted diffusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere with corresponding ADC hypointensity, compatible with acute infarct. Chronic infarct in the right frontal lobe. No hemorrhage on susceptibility images. No mass effect. Ventricles normal in size. Normal flow voids.
reports.conclusion: Small acute infarct, right cerebellar hemisphere. Chronic right frontal infarct.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, regional hospital
Admission 6/1/2026, discharge 6/3/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, right cerebellar hemisphere.
Secondary: prior right frontal ischemic stroke (5/2025), vascular dementia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED with acute vertigo, nausea, gait instability, mild dysarthria and right-sided dysmetria; head CT without hemorrhage. MRI showed a small acute right cerebellar infarct and the old right frontal infarct. Vertigo and nausea settled over the first 36 hours. Walking with PT and his wife at the bedside by day 2; steady enough for home with supervision. Lipids and A1c in range.

Discharge medications:
- NEW: aspirin 81 mg daily
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (unchanged)
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily (unchanged)
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home with wife. PCP visit within 1 week. Stroke neurology clinic in about 6 to 8 weeks. Return for recurrent dizziness, new weakness, speech or swallowing trouble.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called home after 6/1 to 6/3 admission for a small right cerebellar stroke. Spoke with wife. Dizziness much better, no vomiting, he is walking around the house with her nearby. New med: aspirin 81 mg daily, bought OTC and added to his pill box; lisinopril and atorvastatin unchanged. Reviewed when to call 911. TCM visit Tues 6/9 with PCP.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, with wife. Admitted 6/1 to 6/3 for a small acute right cerebellar infarct (records reviewed): sudden vertigo, nausea, slurred speech and right-hand clumsiness at onset, MRI-confirmed.

Since home: no more spinning. A little unsure on his feet the first two days, steadier now. Speech back to his baseline per wife. No headache. Taking aspirin 81 mg plus his usual two meds. No bleeding or bruising. Cognition per wife unchanged from before the admission.

Exam: BP 136/82. Alert, flat affect as before. Speech clear. No nystagmus on primary gaze. Finger-to-nose accurate on both sides. Gait narrow-based and steady.

A/P
1. Acute ischemic stroke, right cerebellum: on aspirin 81 mg daily now. Neurology follow-up in July.
2. Prior right frontal stroke, vascular dementia: wife supervising, no driving.
3. HTN: 136/82 today on lisinopril 20, continue.
4. HLD: atorvastatin 40, continue.
RTC for wellness visit in September or sooner.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
STROKE NEUROLOGY CLINIC, visit 7/20/2026

Dear colleague,

Mr. Rousseau returned with his wife seven weeks after his right cerebellar infarct. The dizziness is fully gone and he is back to walking with her daily. Family describe his memory and initiative as unchanged from the winter.

Medications: aspirin 81 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. NKDA.

Exam: alert, apathetic but engaged. No nystagmus. Finger-to-nose accurate on both sides. Gait steady, able to tandem a few steps.

Impression: recovered from a small right cerebellar infarct; prior right frontal infarct with vascular dementia.

Plan: continue aspirin, atorvastatin and lisinopril. Return in 6 months.

With best regards,
Stroke neurology

documents.title: Aspirin question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Dennis's daughter writing from his account. Quick question. Does Dad need a prescription for the baby aspirin or is the store brand ok? Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Aspirin question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi, no prescription needed. Store-brand 81 mg aspirin is fine, the coated kind, once a day. We'll see him for his wellness visit on September 22.
